title: How Cody Schneider builds marketing agents that run Facebook ads on live business data
summary: Cody defines a real marketing agent as unified data in a warehouse, autonomous decisions on a cadence, and cloud hosting. He walks through a full Facebook ads agent (research, creative, publishing, culling winners) and an AI-for-WordPress startup idea to market with it.

principles.text: A real marketing agent needs unified data, autonomous decisions on a cadence, and cloud hosting; a linear automation workflow is not one.
principles.quote: you have to solve the data problem to like give the agent unified data clarity of like the whole pipeline.

principles.text: Put all channel data (ads, analytics, CRM, Stripe) in one warehouse so the agent can tie a specific ad to revenue.
principles.quote: A data warehouse is a way to unify all of your data sources into a single location so that your agent has the ability to understand all of the data in context

principles.text: Use the Facebook marketing API only for writes (publish, turn off, promote); bulk pulling data breaks TOS and gets accounts banned.
principles.quote: So, how you actually use the Facebook ads API is you use the API only for rights, like only to publish content to the Facebook ads account

principles.text: After Andromeda, skip interest targeting: make creative about a specific pain point and Facebook finds the buyers, making it a strong B2B channel.
principles.quote: Facebook has turned into the best B2B ads channel and that exists right now.

principles.text: Run a test-and-cull loop: publish ads daily, let them run 2 to 3 days, kill losers, and pool winners to compete for budget.
principles.quote: The winning ad sets, they go into a winners pool, and they're competing against each other for the ad budget that's available.

principles.text: Marketing is continuous, not campaign-based; fast feedback loops mean you must observe trends and keep adjusting.
principles.quote: Like how marketing actually functions now is like you're continuously doing this and because the feedback loops are so fast
